summary: Feed s133_double is degraded: 18.4% of TCP sessions are one-way and 38.4% of frames are VXLAN-encapsulated, preventing APM from correlating request/response and parsing overlay transactions.

findings.root_cause: 19 of 103 TCP sessions (18.4%) show traffic in only one direction, typical of asymmetric routing capture or packet broker policy that splits directions across different tool ports/feeds without symmetric flow affinity, or a SPAN/TAP covering only one side of the link.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to measure transaction latency and completion. One-way sessions cause incomplete traces, broken request/response correlation, and inaccurate or missing APM latency/error metrics.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same APM tool port using symmetric hashing so the APM sees complete bidirectional transactions.

findings.root_cause: 568 of 1478 frames (38.4%) arrive inside VXLAN tunnels. Overlay traffic is being mirrored to the tool without decapsulation, so the packet broker is forwarding outer VXLAN headers only.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot parse inner IP/TCP/application headers while encapsulated. Even with needs_full_payload=false, it cannot identify or time inner transactions, creating a 38% visibility blind spot for overlay workloads.

recommended_fix.why: Configure the packet broker to strip VXLAN headers and forward inner packets to the APM so it can decode flows and application transactions.
